$comment: Wire contract for the request body the action POSTs to wpcom/v2/ci-telemetry. Machine-checked by validate.mjs. Types here are the types that must survive into the Logstash properties object, so changing one is an Elasticsearch mapping change, not a rename.

$outcome_notes.$comment: Why the list is longer than the gates suggest.
$outcome_notes.compat_unavailable: Gate 3 fails closed when no direct dependency carries a usable compatibility score, which is a different signal from a score below the threshold. fetch-metadata writes 0 both when the lookup is off and when Dependabot has no score, so this counts the unscored, exactly as cvss_unavailable does for advisories.
$outcome_notes.evaluate_error: The emitter runs under always(), so it also fires when the job errored before reaching a verdict. Without its own outcome those runs would either be lost or miscounted as a gate decision.
$outcome_notes.scheduled_merge_skipped: A candidate whose head commit carries no passing eligibility status. The job warns and moves on, so this is the action working, not a failure.
$outcome_notes.scheduled_merge_revoked: An evaluation withdrew the eligibility evidence while auto-merge was being enabled, so the job disabled it again. Rare, and worth counting because it means two jobs raced.
$outcome_notes.fast_track_refused: Not an outcome. A refused override falls through to the normal gates, so the run still ends in a gate outcome and the refusal rides along as fast_track_refused with a reason.

pr.note: String, not integer. ai_review already maps properties.pr as a string in the shared index.

event_action.note: unlabeled is a caller trigger since QAO-768. Removing the fast-track label has to re-evaluate, or a withdrawn override leaves a queued auto-merge standing.

dependency_type.note: The values fetch-metadata actually emits, not a direct/indirect pair. It reports the most direct type across every updated dependency, so indirect means nothing in the PR is direct. Empty is normalised to unknown by the emitter.

cvss_reported.note: Deliberately a string. Its purpose is to carry the values GitHub sends that are not usable scores, including "", "0.0", "00", ".00" and anything non-numeric. Typing it as a number destroys the exact signal it exists to capture.

cvss_effective.note: Present only when the score was usable. Never 0.

compat_score.note: Present only when a usable score exists. Gate 3 treats 0 as missing data, so 0 never reaches this field.

compat_dependency.note: The direct dependency that decided Gate 3, meaning the lowest scoring one on a pass or a rejection, and the first unscored one when no score was usable.

fast_track_actor.note: The login that applied the fast-track label, resolved from the PR's label history by the authorization check. Already recorded publicly in the audit comment on the PR.

fast_track_role.note: role_name from the collaborator permission lookup, which can be a custom org role, so no enum.

fast_track_refused.note: Boolean rather than a string. properties is JSON encoded before it reaches Elasticsearch, and ai_review already maps properties.is_followup as a boolean, so nested booleans survive. The string rule applies to top-level success, which PHP casts.

auto_merge_revoked.note: The evaluation withdrew an auto-merge this workflow had queued.

forbidden_by_outcome.$comment: Invariants that a payload builder can get wrong silently. An unusable score never becomes the effective score, and a fast-tracked PR never ran a gate at all.
